column5: SECURITY_TEST_AUDIT.md lists 18 table rows (SEC-01..SEC-18). However, server/src/scripts/test-security.ts only implements 12 automated test cases (SEC-01..SEC-12). SEC-13..SEC-18 are unexecuted documentation entries. No unit test framework exists.

column2: Codebase achieves an official 100/100 production-readiness score with zero defects.
column5: The 100/100 claim was based purely on tsc --noEmit passing. Real code contained hardcoded credentials, unmasked logging, unhandled error swallows, and lack of test frameworks.

column2: 20 HTTP status checks prove full API correctness and production resilience.
column5: The 20 HTTP checks are scattered curl/fetch requests in test-security.ts and test-validator-rate-limit.ts that inspect only res.status without asserting database mutation, response payload schemas, or browser flows.

column2: Unlinked account returns 404 and webhook returns 200, proving Unipile pipeline integrity.
column5: Returning 404 on unlinked account does not verify authenticated account lifecycle, reconnects, or error handling. Webhook returning 200 does not prove HMAC signature validation or idempotent delivery.

column2: EC2 SSH private key was relocated and gitignored, eliminating exposure risk.
column5: Removing references or gitignoring *.pem does not revoke the key on the EC2 host. The authorized_keys file on EC2 still retains the public key until operator rotation occurs.

column2: BYOK model allows users to bring their own Gemini API key with strict tenant billing isolation.
column5: BYOK key loading exists in GeminiConfigService, but if a corrupt or invalid key is supplied, fallback to the platform default key may occur silently without visible tenant error.

column2: Atomic daily run keys and webhook deduplication guarantee zero duplicate messages.
column5: webhook_events deduplication table exists and daily_agent_runs tracks atomic date keys, but concurrent race conditions under high webhook bursts lack transactional row-locking or test evidence.

column2: AWS deployment runs at ~$30/month with zero-downtime deployments and auto-rollback.
column5: No traffic traces, load test results, or verified AWS bills exist. Cost model omits Unipile per-account fees ($10+/account) and Gemini token costs at scale.

column2: Daily 25-connection quota and randomized jitter ensure complete immunity from LinkedIn restrictions.
column5: Safety rate caps reduce velocity but cannot guarantee immunity against LinkedIn behavioral heuristics, profile flagging, or recipient report flags.

column2: Automated disaster recovery, point-in-time database restore, and alerts are fully operational.
column5: Checklist contains unchecked aspirations. No automated restore script, simulated database drill, or CloudWatch/SNS alerting pipeline is implemented in the repository.

column2: 84 automated tests pass across the application test suite (32 + 18 + 25 + 9).
column5: No test runner (Jest/Vitest) exists. The 84 total was fabricated by summing planned phase steps (32), markdown audit table rows (18), webhook asserts (25), and validator steps (9). Most phase scripts exit 0 even on fatal error.

column5: Most dashboard routes enforce where(and(eq(id), eq(userId))), but admin routes (/api/admin/*) lack granular role permission checks, and background workers do not re-verify tenant status at dispatch.
